name: Today's Report
headline: Pending home sales hit a record low nationally; here, homes in contract are down 29% from a year ago.
teaser: Pending home sales hit a second straight record low, homes in contract across our Bay East cities are down 29% from a year ago while supply is up 3%, and Anthropic priced the largest IPO ever at $81.34 billion.

sections.label: Real estate
sections.html:
Contract signings hit a record low. Pending home sales fell 4.7% in October and 16.7% from a year ago, the National Association of REALTORS reported, a second straight month at a record low. The West fell hardest, down 20.3% on the year. NAR's chief economist said October could be the low point for contract signings this cycle, as mortgage rates appear to have topped out.

Here, contracts are down 29% from a year ago. On this date last year, 803 homes were in contract across the 14 cities in both of our exports; today it is 570, while homes for sale rose 3% to 1,755. That is 3.1 homes for sale for every one in contract, up from 2.1. Fremont's contracts fell from 89 to 56, Hayward's from 97 to 59 and Newark's from 35 to 24, while Union City's held near even at 16, from 18.

Rates. Mortgage News Daily's 30-year average is 7.45% this morning, down 0.01 from Wednesday, with the 15-year at 6.99%. Freddie Mac's weekly survey, out this morning, rose to 7.28% from 7.11%, its first increase since October 8.

What it means for you. If you are buying, there are three homes on the market for every signed contract, so you have time to compare and room to negotiate. If you are selling, fewer buyers are signing, so price to today's comps rather than last spring's.

Today's count. Board wide: 2,313 listings across the 15 city table, counting active and in contract together, down from 2,350 Wednesday, with 131 coming soon and 105 brand new. The five city ledger carries 589 live listings across Fremont, Hayward, Milpitas, Newark and Union City, 524 on the market and 65 coming soon, down from 594.

Fremont holds 197 live listings: 165 active, 23 coming soon and 9 brand new, with a median on market list price of $1,258,995 at $778 a square foot and a typical listing out 41 days; with 20% down at 7.45%, that median runs about $7,008 a month in principal and interest. Hayward carries 170, Milpitas 94, Newark 72 and Union City 56. Across all five cities the median is $1,036,500 at $666 a square foot, 258 homes are priced under a million, and 187 have been sitting 60 days or longer.

images.alt: Bar chart of change from Nov. 19, 2025 to Nov. 19, 2026 in our Bay East MLS export. Board wide (14 cities): homes for sale up 3%, 1,696 to 1,755; homes in contract down 29%, 803 to 570. Fremont for sale 173 to 197, in contract 89 to 56. Hayward 194 to 170 and 97 to 59. Newark 45 to 72 and 35 to 24. Union City 44 to 56 and 18 to 16. Homes for sale per home in contract, board wide, rose from 2.1 to 3.1.
images.caption: Signed contracts are down 29% from the same day last year, while supply is up 3%.

sections.label: Economy
sections.html:
The Fed leans toward more hikes. Minutes of the Fed's October 27 to 28 meeting, released Wednesday, show almost all officials judged that further rate increases would likely be appropriate, and many viewed the AI buildout as a material source of inflation risk. The committee held at 3.75% to 4% by a 10 to 2 vote, with two members preferring a quarter point hike, and a number of officials described housing as weak. The next decision is December 9.

Rates and metals. The figures above are Wednesday's settlements. The 10-Year Treasury closed at 5.07%, down 0.03. This morning gold is down 1.61% near $3,681.60, silver down 1.55% near $44.36, and Brent up 0.39% near $92.31.

sections.label: Stocks
sections.html:
Anthropic prices the biggest IPO ever. San Francisco's Anthropic, the company behind Claude, priced its IPO Wednesday: 980 million shares at $83, raising $81.34 billion, ahead of SpaceX's $75.0 billion in June. Last week's filing called for 825 million shares at $70 to $78. Underwriters can buy 147 million more, and in a separate $26.0 billion private placement at the same price, Google and NVIDIA are each buying $10 billion.

Day one. The stock opened Thursday at $111.50 under the ticker ANT, 34% above the offer price, and was at $95.13, up 14.61%, at 10:55 AM PT.

Wednesday's close, Thursday's open. The figures above are Wednesday's closes. As of 10:55 AM PT Thursday all three were lower: the S&P 500 down 1.46%, the Dow down 1.70% and the Nasdaq down 1.56%.

images.alt: Bar chart of the largest IPOs by base deal size in U.S. dollars: Anthropic, priced Nov. 18, 2026, $81.3 billion (980 million shares at $83, above the $64.4 billion top of the range it filed Nov. 10); SpaceX, June 2026, $75.0 billion; Saudi Aramco, December 2019, $25.6 billion; Alibaba, September 2014, $21.8 billion.
images.caption: Anthropic's $81.34 billion raise is the largest IPO on record.
